raw_response:
I will keep it simple and practical this year. I am 66, so I will not spread myself across too many crops or take on something that needs a lot of hand labor or market risk. In Quzhou County, I know the wheat-summer maize rotation best, the machines fit it, the inputs are easy to buy, and the grain is easy to sell. So I will stay with winter wheat on my land now, then follow it with summer maize after harvest. I will use improved seed rather than old saved seed because I want steadier emergence, stronger lodging resistance, and less trouble managing the field. I will fertilize at moderate levels instead of pushing for the highest possible yield, because I care more about stable output and controlling cost. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because spring moisture matters a lot for wheat here, and I will keep pesticide use limited to what is needed for the common diseases, insects, and weeds. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is familiar, fast, and workable for me at my age. My goal is not to gamble; my goal is to run a steady grain rotation that I can manage myself and finish on time.
